title: Getting Started with DICi
text: DICi parameterization-invariant, plug--free version Deviance Information Criterion Bayesian model comparison. adds variance-based penalty Gelman et al. (2014) posterior mean deviance, rather unstable plug-deviance used classic DIC: \[\mathrm{DIC}_i = E[D(\theta)] + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Var}[D(\theta)]\] \(D(\theta) = -2 \log f_m(y \mid \theta)\) marginal deviance. penalty \(p_V = \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Var}(D)\) always non-negative, DICi never evaluates deviance point estimate, whole criterion invariant reparameterization. distinguishes DICi related variance-based DIC Gelman et al. (2014), \(\mathrm{DIC}_p = D(\bar\theta) + 2 p_V\), keeps plug-deviance \(D(\bar\theta)\) remains unstable multimodality.

title: Getting Started with DICi
text: core function takes S x N matrix pointwise marginal log-likelihoods (rows = posterior draws, columns = observations):
code: library(DICi)  # Simulate a log-likelihood matrix (S=1000 draws, N=50 observations) set.seed(42) log_lik <- matrix(rnorm(1000 * 50, mean = -2, sd = 0.5), nrow = 1000, ncol = 50)  result <- compute_dic_i(log_lik) print(result) #> Parameterization-Invariant DIC (DIC_i) #> -------------------------------------- #>   DIC_i  = 225.69 #>   p_V    = 25.55 #>   E[D]   = 200.14 #> --------------------------------------

title: Getting Started with DICi
text: Fit multiple candidate models, compute DICi , compare: model lowest DICi preferred. delta_dic_i column shows difference best model.
code: set.seed(123) ll_simple  <- matrix(rnorm(1000 * 50, mean = -2.0, sd = 0.4), 1000, 50) ll_complex <- matrix(rnorm(1000 * 50, mean = -1.9, sd = 0.6), 1000, 50)  fit_simple  <- compute_dic_i(ll_simple) fit_complex <- compute_dic_i(ll_complex)  compare_dic_i(simple = fit_simple, complex = fit_complex) #>     model    dic_i      p_v      e_d delta_dic_i #> 1  simple 215.8741 15.80440 200.0697     0.00000 #> 2 complex 227.7996 38.02143 189.7782    11.92546

title: Stan Workflow: Factor Analysis with Sign Switching
text: key design choice using marginal likelihood. one-factor model, means integrating latent factor analytically: \[\mathbf{y}_j \mid \boldsymbol{\theta} \sim \mathcal{N}_P(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\; \boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{\lambda}^\prime + \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2))\] Stan: generated quantities block outputs pointwise marginal log-likelihoods, compute_dic_i() expects.
code: transformed parameters {   matrix[P, P] V;   V = tcrossprod(to_matrix(lambda, P, 1)) + diag_matrix(square(sigma)); }  model {   alpha ~ normal(0, 5);   lambda ~ normal(0, 1);   // symmetric: allows sign switching   sigma ~ normal(0, 2);    for (j in 1:N) {     Y[j] ~ multi_normal(alpha, V);   } }  generated quantities {   vector[N] log_lik;   for (j in 1:N) {     log_lik[j] = multi_normal_lpdf(Y[j] | alpha, V);   } }

title: Stan Workflow: Factor Analysis with Sign Switching
code: library(cmdstanr) library(DICi)  set.seed(2026) N <- 400; P <- 6 lambda_true <- c(0.81, 0.72, 0.63, 0.54, 0.45, 0.36) alpha_true  <- rep(0, P) sigma_true  <- rep(sqrt(0.5), P)  eta <- rnorm(N) Y <- matrix(NA, N, P) for (j in 1:N) {   Y[j, ] <- alpha_true + lambda_true * eta[j] + rnorm(P, 0, sigma_true) }  mod <- cmdstan_model("fa_marginal.stan") fit <- mod$sample(   data = list(N = N, P = P, Y = Y),   chains = 4, iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,   parallel_chains = 4, seed = 42 )

title: Stan Workflow: Factor Analysis with Sign Switching
code: # One-liner with the cmdstanr wrapper result <- dic_i_from_cmdstanr(fit) print(result) # Parameterization-Invariant DIC (DIC_i) # -------------------------------------- #   DIC_i  = 5724.55 #   p_V    = 17.74 #   E[D]   = 5706.81 # --------------------------------------

title: Stan Workflow: Factor Analysis with Sign Switching
code:
library(loo)  log_lik <- fit$draws("log_lik", format = "draws_matrix") log_lik <- unclass(log_lik)  # WAIC and LOO waic_result <- waic(log_lik) loo_result  <- loo(log_lik)  # Classic DIC D_bar    <- mean(-2 * rowSums(log_lik)) D_plugin <- -2 * sum(colMeans(log_lik)) p_DIC    <- D_bar - D_plugin  cat(sprintf("DIC_i:         %8.1f  (p_V    = %5.1f)
", result$dic_i, result$p_v)) cat(sprintf("WAIC:          %8.1f  (p_WAIC = %5.1f)
",             waic_result$estimates["waic", "Estimate"],             waic_result$estimates["p_waic", "Estimate"])) cat(sprintf("LOO-CV:        %8.1f  (p_LOO  = %5.1f)
",             loo_result$estimates["looic", "Estimate"],             loo_result$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"])) cat(sprintf("DIC (classic): p_DIC = %.1f
", p_DIC)) # Expected output: #   DIC_i, WAIC, LOO-CV all agree closely (~5724-5725) #   p_V, p_WAIC, p_LOO all near true k=18 #   p_DIC is negative (sign switching detected)

text: DICi package computes DICi, parameterization-invariant, plug--free version Deviance Information Criterion comparing latent variable models (Xiao Rabe-Hesketh, 2026, arXiv:2605.27844). DICi adds variance-based penalty \(p_V = \tfrac12 \mathrm{Var}(D)\) Gelman et al. (2014) posterior mean deviance \(E[D(\theta)]\): \[\mathrm{DIC}_i = E[D(\theta)] + \tfrac12 \mathrm{Var}[D(\theta)].\] Unlike classic DIC, DICi never evaluates deviance point estimate, : Never produces negative penalty terms, even sign switching (factor analysis), label switching (mixture models), parameterization switching (overfitted mixtures) depend plug-estimates, destabilized multimodal posteriors asymptotically equivalent WAIC regular, correctly specified models, require pointwise likelihood factorization computationally simple: posterior mean variance marginal deviance needed

title: Compute the Parameterization-Invariant DIC (DIC_i) — compute_dic_i
text: \(\mathrm{DIC}_i\) defined : $$\mathrm{DIC}_i = E_{\theta|y}[D(\theta)] + \frac{1}{2}   \mathrm{Var}_{\theta|y}[D(\theta)]$$ \(D(\theta) = -2 \log f_m(y \mid \theta)\) marginal deviance. criterion adds variance-based penalty \(p_V = \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Var}(D)\) Gelman et al. (2014) posterior mean deviance. terms invariant reparameterization model parameters, \(p_V\) always non-negative. "" \(\mathrm{DIC}_i\) stands (parameterization-)invariant. key difference related variance-based DIC Gelman et al. (2014), denoted \(\mathrm{DIC}_p = D(\bar{\theta}) + 2 p_V\), \(\mathrm{DIC}_i\) uses posterior mean deviance \(E[D(\theta)]\) place plug-deviance \(D(\bar{\theta})\). plug-deviance makes classic DIC (\(\mathrm{DIC}_p\)) unstable multimodality, removing gives \(\mathrm{DIC}_i\) invariance. regular, correctly specified models, \(\mathrm{DIC}_i\) asymptotically equivalent WAIC (Watanabe, 2010) require likelihood factorize independent pointwise contributions.

title: Compute the Parameterization-Invariant DIC (DIC_i) — compute_dic_i
text: meaningful results latent variable models, input must marginal log-likelihoods (integrated latent variables), conditional log-likelihoods (evaluated specific latent variable draws). Stan: code marginal likelihood model block (e.g., using log_sum_exp mixtures multivariate normal density integrating random effects) output pointwise contributions generated quantities, extracted log-likelihoods marginal. recommended workflow. JAGS/BUGS: programs typically sample latent variables report conditional likelihoods. use \(\mathrm{DIC}_i\), need compute marginal likelihood , requires model-specific integration (analytic linear mixed models, numerical otherwise). Mplus: marginal deviance reported directly. Use deviance_draws argument pass deviance values. discussion marginal vs. conditional likelihoods Bayesian model comparison, see Merkle, Furr, Rabe-Hesketh (2019).

title: Compute the Parameterization-Invariant DIC (DIC_i) — compute_dic_i
code: # Simulate fake log-likelihood matrix (S=1000 draws, N=50 observations) set.seed(42) S <- 1000 N <- 50 log_lik <- matrix(rnorm(S * N, mean = -2, sd = 0.5), nrow = S, ncol = N)  result <- compute_dic_i(log_lik) result$dic_i #> [1] 225.6861 result$p_v #> [1] 25.54797 result$e_d #> [1] 200.1382  # Using pre-computed deviance draws dev_draws <- -2 * rowSums(log_lik) result2 <- compute_dic_i(deviance_draws = dev_draws) all.equal(result$dic_i, result2$dic_i) #> [1] TRUE
